fr.recommendations:
• Install reflective address markers at both the entry and exit points of the circular driveway so responders can identify the correct approach and departure routes at night.
• Mark which driveway opening is the preferred entry point for emergency vehicles to prevent confusion on approach.
• Trim vegetation along the access drive to maintain a clear overhead and lateral path for emergency vehicles.
• Cut back dense vegetation near the structure to keep a clear path along the exterior walls for responders moving around the building.
• Clear a defined walking path along the sides of the structure so responders can reach the rear of the property without pushing through dense growth.
• Trim any shrubs or low branches along the perimeter fencing line that would slow or block responder movement between the front and rear of the property.
• Keep the access drive surface free of parked vehicles, equipment, or debris so it remains open for emergency vehicle staging.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim branches and shrubs that are directly touching or overhanging the house on all sides.
• Thin the tree clusters near the structure to create open space between individual trees and between the trees and the house.
• Remove shrubs and low-growing plants from beneath the large trees closest to the house.
• Separate shrubs and plants along the base of the house by pulling them back several feet from the walls.
• Thin scattered trees across the property so they do not form a continuous canopy leading directly to the house.
• Clear overhanging branches along the driveway so vehicles, including fire trucks, can pass without obstruction.
• Remove shrubs and plants growing along the edges of the driveway that narrow the travel lane.
• Trim low branches on large trees near the house up from the ground to reduce the chance of fire climbing into the canopy.
• Thin scattered shrubs across the property so plants are not growing close enough together to carry fire toward the house.
• Keep the open green space free of dead plant material, fallen branches, and leaf litter.
• Create visible open gaps between tree clusters and the structure by removing the trees or shrubs that fill in those gaps.
• Remove dead wood, fallen limbs, and dry leaf buildup beneath all trees and shrubs near the house.
